passage: Tenzin had done everything that was expected: finished his degree, passed the bank exam, come home to the hill town with a steady job and a scarf from his mother. And now, on the evening bus back from the branch, he thought, is this it? The mountains looked the same as ever. At night he scrolled for hours until his eyes stung, and woke up feeling as though nothing had happened at all. On Sunday Binita, who ran the little village library from her verandah, asked him to help read stories to eight children who couldn't yet manage on their own. He said he was rubbish at it. He went anyway. The children argued over the yak story. Tenzin laughed properly for the first time in weeks, then wondered what else he might try.

qa.q: Where did Binita run the little library?
qa.a: Binita ran it from her verandah.

qa.q: What was Tenzin worried about on the bus home?
qa.a: Tenzin was worried that this steady job might be all there was, and unsure what it was all for.

qa.q: What small step helped Tenzin begin to find direction?
qa.a: He tried helping Binita read stories to children, which led him to laugh and wonder what else to try.

qa.q: How might Binita see Tenzin's reluctance to help?
qa.a: Binita probably sees it as ordinary self-doubt, and invited him because trying something is how purpose starts.

grounding: After doing what he was supposed to do, the protagonist feels empty and numbs with scrolling; a small experiment of helping others opens a path.

passage:
Vaibhav, you asked me on the show what nobody tells you after the big goal. It's Chandrika here, twenty-two, and last year I did everything right. Engineering degree, campus placement, the job in the glass building. My parents distributed sweets. And by March I was lying on my bed every evening scrolling until two, wondering: is this it? What is any of this for?

I kept waiting to find my purpose, like it was a lost wallet.

What changed was small. A colleague asked me to cover her Saturday slot at a children's reading hour in the public library. I went, grumbling. A boy of eight read a whole page aloud for the first time and looked at me like I'd given him a medal.

I went back the next Saturday. Then I tried a pottery class, which I was terrible at. I'm still trying things. Purpose didn't arrive. It's growing, one Saturday at a time.

qa.q: Where did Chandrika cover a colleague's Saturday slot?
qa.a: At a children's reading hour in the public library.

qa.q: How did Chandrika feel in the evenings by March?
qa.a: Chandrika felt empty and lost, scrolling until two and wondering what everything was for.

qa.q: What helped Chandrika more than waiting to find a purpose?
qa.a: Trying small things, like the reading hour and a pottery class, let purpose grow from action.

qa.q: How might the boy who read a whole page see Chandrika?
qa.a: The boy seemed proud and grateful, seeing Chandrika as someone who helped him achieve something big.

grounding: The monologue shows a young person who did everything expected and felt empty, finding purpose through small experiments and helping others instead of numbing.

passage:
July. Darshan had his degree, a certificate in a plastic sleeve, and no idea what came next. He woke at noon in his parents' flat in Vadodara, scrolled short videos until evening, and felt nothing much at all.

August, a Wednesday. Hansa ben, who ran the community kitchen in the temple compound, caught him on the stairs. "You have free hands. We are short of people to chop vegetables on Wednesdays." He said yes mostly to escape.

October. He had not missed a Wednesday. He'd learned to cut onions without crying, and an old man named Mohanbhai told him stories about the textile mills while they worked. Last week, Hansa ben asked him to help set up a spreadsheet for donations. He stayed three hours. On the bus home he realised he hadn't opened the video app all day.

He still didn't know what his life was for. But Wednesdays had a point.

qa.q: Where did Hansa ben run the community kitchen?
What was Darshan feeling in July?
qa.a: Darshan felt empty and aimless, scrolling all day and feeling nothing much at all.

qa.q: What helped Darshan begin to feel purpose?
qa.a: Saying yes to chopping vegetables every Wednesday, meeting people and helping with the donations spreadsheet let purpose grow from action.

qa.q: How might Hansa ben see Darshan by October?
qa.a: Hansa ben seems to see him as reliable and capable, trusting him with the donations spreadsheet.

grounding: The three beats show a young man feeling empty after doing what was expected, letting purpose emerge through helping and meeting people.
